newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Quiet Swedish shares ease, waiting for Nokia.
newsitem.headline: Quiet Swedish shares ease, waiting for Nokia.

text.p: Swedish share prices recovered somewhat following an early fall on Monday.
At 1000 GMT the market's general index had fallen 0.12 percent to 3,154.54 in light turnover of 781 million crowns.
Telecoms group Ericsson lost ground after losses overnight in New York. The share was trading down 3.5 crowns at 358, after closing at the equivalent of about 357 crowns on Wall Street on Friday.
The market was looking for Nokia's half-year figures due at 1300 GMT. Nokia was expected to show H1 profits rising to 3.09 billion markka from 1.13 billion a year ago.
"Nokia's report is the key to how Ericsson will close today -- maybe even the entire market," one broker said.
Truckmaker Scania was also due to post half-year earnings, around 1030 GMT. The share was trading half a crown higher at 225.5 compared to 227 crowns at the market's open.

"A rumour is going around that the report is going to be somewhat lower than expected," one broker said. Scania was expected to post a profit after financial items of 1.43 billion crowns against 2.10 billion a year earlier.
Drug company Astra was underpinning the market, with the share trading up 2.5 crowns to 144.5.
